disagreements.target: ESCALATION-RULINGS D-005 (and R33-03, C-1, the 57/39/38 expected counts)
disagreements.review_position: F019 p1 revision is PRESENT '00' (the title-block 'Rev. no.' cell), association resolved, not excluded. F019 revision is yes/yes, the revision population goes 38 -> 39, and reviewed-2 expects 57/39/38. Basis: frozen section 4 names the cell the primary source, so the frozen text decides and section 2 'ambiguous' does not apply. '01' is disclosed as a plausible prediction, and F019 is to be named a contested row.
disagreements.critic_view: Rule D-005 AMBIGUOUS, with candidates 00 (the cell) and 01 (the latest table entry), excluded. F019 revision is then no/no and the revision population stays 38. Keep PRESENT '00' only as the owner alternative. (1) The frozen text itself points to ambiguous. Section 4's primary source is 'the page's own CURRENT revision, from its revision cell'. On this page, the revision table's latest row (REV 01, 09-05-16, AS PER CONSULTANT COMMENTS) carries the same date as the title-block DATE (09-05-16). So the page does not establish that the cell shows the current revision, and frozen section 2 defines ambiguous as a case where 'which of several candidates is the field cannot be established from the page'. The R32 dispositions agent recorded exactly that ('The image does not settle which revision is current', DISPOSITIONS D-005), and the draft concedes the same when it calls '01' plausible. Reaching ambiguous therefore needs no topic (i) amendment. (2) The cost is lopsided. Under the frozen stop rules (DRAFT-DECLARATION.v2 stop_rules; STOP-AND-SAFETY-RULES lines 9-12), a critical acceptance on RESOLVED truth makes B terminal with the comparison INVALID, or makes C terminal with the result 'candidate failed the safety gate'. A critical acceptance on unresolved truth is only reported. Revision is a critical field (AI-ACCURACY-POLICY line 60: 'Verify critical identity/revision/decision facts'). Turning a row the review itself calls contested into resolved truth creates a known path to a terminal stop or an INVALID comparison, and a disclosure cannot neutralise it. Revision is 38 >= 12 either way, so making the row scorable gains nothing at the gate. F019 is also a decision-bearing document (decision present/resolved), so it is likely to enter the 16-document run set.
disagreements.why_material: Adopting it changes an escalation ruling (D-005 PRESENT -> AMBIGUOUS) and a count: revision after reviewed-2 is 38, not 39, so reviewed-2 expects 57/38/38, not 57/39/38. It also changes required action C-1: the rows to write change, F019 revision is excluded, and the 'contested row' disclosure becomes an excluded-row disclosure. The verdict category does not change.

disagreements.target: R33-02 / condition C-3 (and the R33-26 assurance wording)
disagreements.review_position: Policy section 8 conflicts with labels made only by Claude. The owner resolves it by an append-only amendment or waiver, or by a human check of the rows that will be scored. Label truth is accepted on the strength of a 98-item image check with 0 rows refuted.
disagreements.critic_view: The draft leaves out the fact that matters most to the owner's choice: the model under evaluation is from the same family as every label agent. The AI ledger (read-only) shows that the evaluated extraction requests used Claude models: claude-sonnet-5 457 entries, claude-opus-5 5, 'sonnet' 13, blank 8. The drafter, the seven R32 batch reviewers, the consolidator, critic and disposer, all Review 33 dimension agents and this critic are Claude Opus 5.5. Section 8's 'approved solely by another model' bites hardest exactly here. Shared reading errors between labeller and predictor inflate agreement and can hide the critical false acceptances that the zero-critical gate exists to catch. The D3 check does not remove this risk: it is the same model re-reading the pages, and it rechecked about 46 of roughly 382 accept rows (0 refuted gives a 95% upper bound near 6.5%). Required action C-3 should do three things. (a) State the same-family fact explicitly to the owner. (b) Name as the recommended route a human check of every page-field row that will actually be scored in the frozen run set (at most 30 documents, at most 120 pages), done after the selector freezes and before B runs, with a waiver only as the fallback. (c) Have the declaration state the assurance level: AI-drafted, AI-reviewed, and from the same model family as the system under test.
disagreements.why_material: It changes the content of required action C-3 and adds a disclosure to C-7. Severity (major) and verdict are unchanged.

disagreements.target: R33-08 / condition C-7 / draft section 5.2 (declaration bindings)
disagreements.review_position: Section 5.2 lists the bindings the final declaration must replace or add: labels, population, cohort and selection, staging, run set, harness, caps and authorization.
disagreements.critic_view: Two bindings are missing. (1) AI-ACCURACY-POLICY section 7 requires the experiment record, before execution, to hold 'source/truth hashes, selected files and project AI policies', and to use 'project-policy-eligible documents'. No Review 33 dimension or the draft checks or binds the AI policy and eligibility of EP-3563, 22349, 27331, 15744, 26687 and 29255. ORCH-001 records that the live application database holds none of the cohort projects, so the sandbox policy must be declared explicitly. (2) BINDING-MANIFEST.json binds AI-ACCURACY-POLICY.md at 7efa891b..., and DRAFT-DECLARATION.v2 thresholds_verbatim quotes it by hash. If C-3 is met by an append-only amendment to that file, the hash changes and the preflight ('any difference refuses the run') fails unless the policy is re-bound. In addition, the expected-use estimates in DRAFT-DECLARATION.v2 (B about 6, C about 135, R about 10, P about 20) came from the four-arm sample and must be re-estimated for the r32 run set.
disagreements.why_material: It adds required declaration bindings to C-7 and an owner-facing check (project AI policies) before any live run. Verdict and severities are unchanged.
disagreements.evidence: AI-ACCURACY-POLICY.md section 7 lead-in (lines 78-80) and the paragraph 'Use isolated copies and project-policy-eligible documents'. sha256 of AI-ACCURACY-POLICY.md recomputed as 7efa891b55fd6a4113f08cff8d0acdca7832d611524bb7f884ec4e5bc30a4f47, equal to review31/BINDING-MANIFEST.json line 86. disagreements.target: Condition C-2 / R33-04 / ESCALATION-RULINGS carried_over count-once F031->F001, F059->F046
disagreements.review_position: Count-once (c)(ii) is 'defensible' but an unrecorded amendment. C-2 offers two routes: record it as an amendment, or revert to byte-identical-only counting (59/40/39). In the same draft, section 1 says the verdict accepts 'the counted populations, 57/38/38'.
disagreements.critic_view: The draft accepts counts that depend on a rule it declines to rule on. NEXT-BOUNDED-TASK requires Review 33 to 'rule on ... the carried-over convention items with page evidence', and the review ruled D-004 and D-005 with the same authority. It should rule (c)(ii) the same way: ADOPTED for this cohort as a Review 33 ruling, with the F031 p3 caveat. Then C-2 becomes a recording step in reviewed-2 and the declaration, not an open choice. If the review will not rule, it should accept the populations only conditionally, in the form '57/38/38 under (c)(ii), or 59/40/39 without it'. The page evidence supports adoption: R33-CRITIC confirmed 0 differing pixels for F001/F031 p1 and p2, and for F046/F059 a difference confined to a seal outside the title block, with identical title blocks.
disagreements.why_material: It changes required action C-2 (an open alternative becomes a ruling) and removes an internal inconsistency in what the verdict accepts. The gate passes either way, so the verdict is unchanged.

disagreements.review_position: The stratum leg 'makes decision ELIGIBLE unreachable' and very likely fires for identity and revision.
disagreements.critic_view: The effect is wider than one field. score_bcr.evaluate collects every field's concentration flag into a single reasons_not_eligible list, and it sets one outcome for the whole comparison. So any positive decision net gain (except a net gain of 2 split 1/1 with F072) makes the whole candidate NOT ELIGIBLE, not only the decision field. Perversely, C can be ELIGIBLE only if it does not improve decision. The C-4 owner card should say this plainly.
disagreements.why_material: R33-01 is already major and C-4 already puts the decision to the owner. Only the description of impact changes.
disagreements.evidence: review31/scripts/harness/score_bcr.py lines 198-208 (concentration) and 255-268 (reasons appended per field; outcome 'NOT ELIGIBLE' if any reason). Decision strata recounted by R33-CRITIC: review_signal 37, other 1 (F072).

summary: R33-CRITIC does not challenge the verdict category PREPARATION ACCEPTED WITH CONDITIONS. Every binding recomputes; the populations recount to 57/38/38 (raw 59/40/39); 72 of 72 originals are unchanged by os.stat; sealed projects are disjoint; the ledger stands at 483/17/0; and the D-004 outcome is confirmed on the images. There are 13 disagreements, 5 of them material. (C-001) D-005 should be AMBIGUOUS, not PRESENT '00'. The page does not establish the current revision (table row 01 carries the title-block date), and contested truth made resolved is a direct path to a terminal stop or an INVALID comparison under the frozen stop rules. Revision then stays 38 and reviewed-2 expects 57/38/38. (C-002) C-3 must state that the evaluated model is from the same Claude family as every label agent, and should recommend a human check of the frozen run-set rows. (C-003) R33-05 should read 25 documents, not 27. (C-004) The declaration must bind the project AI policies (policy section 7) and re-bind the policy hash if section 8 is amended. (C-005) Review 33 should rule count-once (c)(ii) adopted, rather than accept 57/38/38 while leaving a revert option open. Nothing in the draft authorizes a run, budget, ledger scope, default, M2 acceptance or M3. M2 remains CHANGES STILL REQUIRED, and M3 has not started. This critique is an owner-delegated independent Claude AI review, not human sign-off.
